body.text: Today we start connecting thoughts and feelings to sleep. Sleep diary first.
Your thoughts, feelings and emotions have a direct connection with your sleep. Negative thoughts heighten alertness and delay sleep. Calmer thoughts do the opposite.
This is the feedback loop we'll start tracking: your mindset shapes your rest, and your rest shapes tomorrow's mindset.

blocks.title: Mental Mirror

body.text: Which of these felt true this morning?

quoteText: 😊 Woke up refreshed 💤 Slept soundly, uninterrupted🤸 Tossed and turned 😨 Mind was racing with worries💢 Woke up groggy / low mood🔋 Feel rested and energized😪 Still feel tired🫂 Feel good, body thanks me

body.text: Thanks for the honesty! Tomorrow we shall go a layer deeper.
Sleep diary, then straight into today's topic.

A thought is a sentence in your head, like "This line is taking forever", whereas a feeling is usually a one-word reaction to that thought, say bored or anxious. Telling them apart helps you see why you reacted the way you did.

For each situation below, one line is a thought, one is a feeling. We have done the first one for you. Frequent power cuts → "They make me furious!" = Feeling; "They make things inconvenient for a lot of us." = Thought

body.text: Racing thoughts at night? Journaling may just be your secret weapon. Think of it as a release valve. Set a 5-minute timer, open a blank page, and write down every thought without any editing. Once the timer's up, you don't need to reread it. The point is emptying, not analyzing.

notes.text: Show a card, user picks a date then writes what happened/thought.
User can add cards for as many items as they feel like. Cards can be pulled up by swiping left or right.

body.text: However that felt, you did it. Tomorrow we’ll look at what actually distracts you from sleep.
Welcome back! As always, sleep diary first.

Poor sleep usually comes from two places: trouble falling asleep, or poor quality once you're out. Both are driven by distractions. Some are within our control, like phone usage, bedtime and racing thoughts, and some are beyond it, like a dog barking, room temperature or a snoring partner.

body.text: Now that we know what to target, we’ll brainstorm fixes tomorrow. Stay tuned!
Sleep diary first.

Today is all about brainstorming, not solving. Example: if phone use is the culprit, ideas might range from "keep it in another room" to "download a lock app" to "buy an alarm clock." No idea is too small or too obvious yet.
No idea is wrong • Don't critique while writing • Write everything down • Build on your own ideas • Stay on topic • Respect the timer

Disturbance: doomscrolling on Instagram → Ideas: uninstall it nightly • keep phone in another room • use night mode • quit the app entirely. (We'll refine these later — for now, quantity over quality.)

body.text: Take the rest of the day off from this. Tomorrow we turn ideas into a plan.
Welcome back! Before we begin, let’s fill the sleep diary.

Not every idea from your brainstorm is realistic. We've pulled in your list for you to weigh the pros and cons of each in order to land on a balanced solution for all your disturbances. Continuing with our earlier example of doomscrolling → uninstall nightly (pro: cuts the biggest distraction / con: a hassle) → keep phone away (pro: blocks other distractions too / con: my alarm's on my phone) → night mode (pro: easier on the eyes / con: doesn't stop the scrolling) → quit entirely (pro: biggest impact / con: too extreme, I use it to stay in touch). Balanced fix: get a separate alarm clock, keep the phone away from the bed.

Sleep diary first.

A consistent pre-sleep routine tells your nervous system and your body it's time to wind down. It's also a good place to fit in essentials like medication, washing up, or just decompressing after a stressful day.

body.text: From what you picked, choose what you'll actually try tonight. A few non-negotiables that help almost everyone:
No caffeine within 4 hours of bed
No exercise within 3 hours of bed
Lights dimmed 30 min before bed
No phone in the last 30 min before bed

body.text: Now that we’ve come up with a list of rituals, we’ll work on making it stick from tomorrow onwards.
First things first, let’s fill the sleep diary.

Knowing the technique isn't the hard part. Following through every day is. Distractions and broken routines get in the way of almost everyone. We'll take it one small step at a time, starting with a technique called piggybacking.
First: list everything you do in a day, start to finish, from brushing your teeth, commuting, cooking, filing reports, all of it. Even the small stuff counts.

body.text: Pick one thing you already do every day, ideally near the end of it, say, clearing the dinner table. For the next week, do your new habit immediately after that anchor activity, no distractions. Miss a day? That’s alright, just don't miss two in a row.
